page.title: Marbella Yacht Charter License Requirements 2032: Updated Rules

data.meta_description: Need a license to charter a yacht in Marbella in 2032? Updated rules for skippered boats, bareboat rentals & Puerto Banús. Read the guide now.
data.summary: A clear breakdown of Marbella yacht charter license requirements for 2032, covering skippered vs bareboat rentals, the updated Spanish maritime regulations, and what you need to know before booking in Puerto Banús.
key_facts: No license needed for skippered charters (all our boats include a licensed skipper).
Bareboat rental (without skipper) requires a Spanish recreational boating license or an ICC.
Skippered charters cover insurance, fuel, taxes, and safety gear – no hidden extras.
Minimum age for skipper-less rental is 18; license must be valid for the boat's length and power.
Puerto Banús departures: all boats in our fleet are skippered, so no license is required.
2032 update: Spain still accepts ICC from RYA, US Sailing, and equivalent national bodies.
Non-EU licenses may need a translation or official endorsement – check before your trip.

faq.q: Do I need a license to charter a yacht in Marbella in 2032?
faq.a: No, if you book a skippered charter (which all our boats are). The licensed skipper handles navigation, mooring, and safety. You just relax. For bareboat rentals (without a skipper), you need a Spanish recreational boating license or an International Certificate of Competence (ICC).

faq.q: What is the ICC and is it accepted in Spain?
faq.a: The International Certificate of Competence (ICC) is a standard document proving you can operate a pleasure craft. Spain accepts ICCs issued by recognised bodies such as the UK's Royal Yachting Association (RYA), US Sailing, and most European national authorities. It must cover the type and size of boat you intend to charter.

faq.q: Can I use my US boating license in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, but it must be accompanied by an ICC or a certified translation into Spanish. US Sailing issues ICCs for American residents. Without one, you may not be allowed to charter bareboat. Our advice: book a skippered charter and skip the paperwork.

faq.q: What if I have a UK RYA Day Skipper qualification?
faq.a: An RYA Day Skipper certificate is widely respected but does not automatically equal an ICC. You can apply for an ICC from the RYA if you hold the appropriate practical certificate. Alternatively, just book a skippered charter – no license needed.

faq.q: Are there age restrictions for chartering without a license?
faq.a: Yes. For bareboat charters (if you had a license), the minimum age is 18. For skippered charters, there is no minimum age for passengers; children are welcome on most boats. The skipper is responsible for all safety and navigation.

faq.q: Do I need a special license for jet skis in Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Yes. Jet ski hire in Spain requires a specific recreational license (PER or PNB) or an ICC with a jet ski endorsement. However, our Mangusta 80 charters (€4,719/4h) include a jet ski as a water toy, operated by the skipper – so you don't need a license to use it.

faq.q: What documents do I need to bring on the day?
faq.a: For skippered charters, just a valid ID or passport for each guest. No boating documents required. If you somehow arranged a bareboat charter, you'd need your license, ICC, passport, and proof of insurance. But we only offer skippered boats – so pack your sunscreen, not your paperwork.

faq.q: Will the 2032 rules change anything for my booking?
faq.a: No. The 2032 update mainly clarifies that Spain continues to recognise ICCs from RYA, US Sailing, and EU authorities. There are no new restrictions for skippered charters. Your booking with us remains license-free, with a professional skipper and all inclusions covered.

data.body_html:
If you're planning a day on the water in Marbella, the first question is often: do I need a licence to charter a yacht? The short answer is no – not if you book a skippered charter, which is what we offer from Puerto Banús. But the full picture includes a few nuances, especially with the updated Spanish maritime regulations for 2032. This guide covers everything you need to know about Marbella yacht charter license requirements 2032, so you can book with confidence.

Do you need a license for a yacht charter in Marbella?

No. All our charter boats come with a licensed skipper included in the price. That means you don't need any boating qualification, ICC, or Spanish permit. The skipper handles navigation, mooring, safety, and fuel. You just enjoy the Costa del Sol from the water. This applies to every boat in our fleet – from the Astondoa 40 (€749/2h) to the Mangusta 80 (€4,719/4h).

What about bareboat charters?

Bareboat rentals (no skipper) are rare in Marbella for day charters. If you did want one, you'd need a Spanish recreational boating license or an International Certificate of Competence (ICC) valid for the boat's length and power. The ICC is accepted across Spain under the 2032 rules, as long as it's issued by a recognised authority like the RYA (UK), US Sailing, or an EU equivalent. Non-EU licenses may need a certified translation. But honestly – why bother? Our skippered charters are simpler and safer.

Which boats require a license?

None of our boats require a license from you, because every charter includes a skipper. But if you're curious: boats over 6 metres or with engines over 15 kW (20 hp) generally require a license for bareboat operation. Our smallest boats – the Dubhe (8m) and Mariah SX21 (6.4m) – fall into that category. With a skipper, there's no issue.

What's included in a skippered charter?

Every charter includes: licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs. You don't need to bring a thing except your ID and sunscreen. The skipper knows the best anchorages – Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, or a cruise past the Golden Mile – and handles all the details.

2032 rule changes: what's different?

The 2032 update is mostly a clarification, not a revolution. Spain has confirmed it continues to recognise ICCs from RYA, US Sailing, and EU bodies. There's no new requirement for skippered charter passengers to hold any license. The rules mainly affect bareboat operators and private boat owners. For holidaymakers, nothing changes – you can still book a skippered yacht from Puerto Banús without paperwork.

What about jet skis and water toys?

Jet skis in Spain require a specific license (PER or PNB) or an ICC with a jet ski endorsement. But on our Mangusta 80 charters (€4,719/4h), a jet ski is included as a water toy – operated by the skipper. So you can ride it without a license. Same goes for paddleboards and snorkel gear on other boats – all supervised by the crew.
